title: WIPPES Act
official_title: To require certain products to be labeled with "Do Not Flush" labeling, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Received in the Senate on June 24, 2025 following House action. Sponsored by a Republican member with seven cosponsors and referred in the House to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: Establishes a federal "Do Not Flush" labeling regime for premoistened, nonwoven disposable wipes marketed as baby or diapering wipes, and for household or personal-care wipes that are composed entirely or in part of petrochemical-derived fibers and have significant potential to be flushed (including antibacterial and disinfecting wipes, general and bathroom cleaning wipes, and body/personal-care wipes such as hand sanitizing, makeup removal, feminine and adult hygiene, and body cleansing). Covered entities (manufacturers, wholesalers, suppliers, individuals, or retailers responsible for the labeling or retail packaging of a covered product sold or offered for retail sale in the United States) must display both the phrase "Do Not Flush" (the "label notice") and the INDA/EDANA "Do Not Flush" symbol clearly and conspicuously in accordance with packaging-type rules. For cylindrical/near-cylindrical dispensing packages, the symbol and label notice must appear on the principal display panel or, alternatively, the symbol appears on the panel while the label notice (or combination) covers at least 8 percent of the flip lid. Flexible film packaging, rigid/refillable packaging, packaging not intended to dispense individual wipes, and bulk retail packaging each have their own placement rules. Outer packaging of combined products is exempt (with an accommodation for combined-product packages smaller than 3 inches by 3 inches). The symbol and label notice must each be equal in size to at least 2 percent of the principal display panel's surface area, and must have a contrast percentage of at least 70 percent against the background — light-on-dark or dark-on-light — except an embossed symbol or label notice on the flip lid of cylindrical or near-cylindrical packaging is exempt from the contrast rule. Covered entities may not make any express or implied representation that a covered product can or should be flushed. The Federal Trade Commission enforces the section: a violation is treated as a violation of a regulation under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B)) regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices, and the FTC may promulgate implementing regulations under section 553 of title 5, U.S.C., consulting with EPA, FDA, and the Consumer Product Safety Commission as appropriate. State laws that are not identical to the federal requirements are preempted. The section applies to covered entities beginning 1 year after the date of enactment.
brief: Requires baby/diapering wipes and specified household or personal-care wipes made even partly of petrochemical fibers to carry a "Do Not Flush" label notice and the INDA/EDANA symbol on packaging (with specific placement, size, and contrast rules), bars flushability claims, gives the FTC enforcement authority, preempts non-identical State laws, and takes effect 1 year after enactment.

top_lines.headline: Federal "Do Not Flush" Label + Symbol Requirement
subs: Covered entities must label covered products clearly and conspicuously with both the "Do Not Flush" label notice and the INDA/EDANA symbol
Covered entities may not make any express or implied representation that a covered product can or should be flushed

top_lines.headline: Placement Rules by Packaging Type
subs: Cylindrical dispensing packaging: symbol + label notice on principal display panel — or symbol on panel with label notice (or combination) covering at least 8 percent of the flip lid
Flexible film dispensing packaging: symbol on principal display panel and on dispensing side panel if different; label notice on principal display panel or dispensing side panel
Rigid/refillable dispensing packaging: symbol + label notice on principal display panel visible each time a wipe is dispensed
Packaging not intended to dispense individual wipes: symbol + label notice on principal display panel visible to the user
Bulk retail: symbol + label notice on both outer packaging and individual packaging, with two enumerated exemptions
Combined-product packaging: outer packaging exempt; individual covered-product packages smaller than 3 by 3 inches may satisfy the requirement with prominent placement

top_lines.headline: Size + Contrast Standards
subs: Symbol and label notice each must equal at least 2 percent of the principal display panel's surface area
Contrast percentage of at least 70 percent between symbol/notice and immediate background, using the formula (B1 − B2) / B1 × 100 where B1 and B2 are light reflectance values
Light on dark or dark on light
Embossed symbol or label notice on the flip lid of a cylindrical or near-cylindrical package is exempt from the contrast rule

top_lines.headline: FTC Enforcement + State Preemption
subs: Violations treated as violations of a regulation under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B)) — unfair or deceptive acts or practices
FTC enforcement with same jurisdiction, powers, and duties as under the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.)
FTC may promulgate regulations under section 553 of title 5, U.S.C., and may consult with EPA, FDA, or the Consumer Product Safety Commission
State or local requirements not identical to the federal requirements are preempted

items.main: Names the Act the "Wastewater Infrastructure Pollution Prevention and Environmental Safety Act" or the "WIPPES Act."
items.detail: Short-title section only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Requires covered entities to label covered products clearly and conspicuously with both the label notice ("Do Not Flush") and the symbol (the INDA/EDANA "Do Not Flush" symbol from the most recent edition of the Guidelines for Assessing the Flushability of Disposable Nonwoven Products, or an FTC-adopted equivalent).
items.detail: Subsection (a) sets the core labeling duty. Definitions in subsection (g) tie "label notice" to the phrase "Do Not Flush" and "symbol" to the INDA/EDANA depiction.

items.main: Placement rules vary by packaging type: cylindrical dispensing packaging must display both on the principal display panel or, alternatively, the symbol on the panel with the label notice (or combination) covering at least 8 percent of the flip lid; flexible film dispensing packaging requires the symbol on the principal display panel and on the dispensing side panel if different, with the label notice on either; rigid/refillable dispensing packaging requires both on the principal display panel visible each time a wipe is dispensed; non-dispensing packaging requires both on the principal display panel; bulk retail requires both on outer and individual packaging (with two enumerated exemptions); combined-product outer packaging is exempt, and combined-product packages under 3 by 3 inches may satisfy the requirement with prominent placement.
items.detail: Subsection (b) contains the placement rules across six enumerated packaging categories.

items.main: Reasonable visibility: symbol and label notice must not be obscured by packaging seams, folds, or design elements; each must equal at least 2 percent of the principal display panel's surface area; each must have high contrast (at least 70 percent contrast percentage under the (B1 − B2) / B1 × 100 formula) with the immediate background — light on dark or dark on light. An embossed symbol or label notice on the flip lid of a cylindrical or near-cylindrical package is exempt from the contrast rule. The symbol and label notice may be adjacent or on separate areas of the principal display panel.
items.detail: Subsection (c) sets the size and contrast standards.

items.main: Prohibits covered entities from making any express or implied representation that a covered product can or should be flushed.

FTC enforcement: a violation of the section or an implementing regulation is treated as a violation of a regulation under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B)) regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices. The Commission enforces with the same jurisdiction, powers, and duties as under the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.), and violators are subject to the same penalties. The Commission may promulgate implementing regulations under section 553 of title 5, U.S.C., and may consult with the EPA Administrator, the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, the Consumer Product Safety Commission, or any other agency as appropriate. Nothing limits the Commission's other statutory authority.
items.detail: Subsection (e) is the enforcement and rulemaking framework.

items.main: State-law preemption: no State or political subdivision may establish or continue in effect requirements with respect to the "Do Not Flush" labeling of covered products that are not identical to the federal requirements and implementing regulations.

Definitions in subsection (g) — including "covered product" (premoistened, nonwoven disposable wipes marketed as baby or diapering wipes, or household/personal care wipes composed entirely or in part of petrochemical-derived fibers and having significant potential to be flushed, with named inclusions covering antibacterial, disinfecting, general/bathroom cleaning, and personal-care wipes such as hand sanitizing, makeup removal, feminine hygiene, adult hygiene, and body cleansing); "combined product" (two or more products in shared retail packaging where at least one is a covered product and at least one is a consumer product intended to be used with it); "covered entity" (a manufacturer, wholesaler, supplier, individual or group of individuals, or retailer responsible for the labeling or retail packaging of a covered product sold or offered for retail sale in the U.S.); "high contrast," "label notice," "principal display panel," "State," and "symbol."
Effective date: section applies to covered entities beginning on the date that is 1 year after the date of enactment.

gaps: The bill does not authorize any civil penalty amounts specific to this section — it relies on the general penalty structure under the FTC Act.
The bill does not define "significant potential to be flushed," leaving that judgment to covered entities and, ultimately, FTC enforcement.
The bill does not describe how existing State "Do Not Flush" labeling laws (already in place in some States) transition to the federal identical-requirement standard.
The bill does not set a deadline within which the FTC must issue implementing regulations.

added: Federal "Do Not Flush" label notice and symbol requirement for covered wipes, effective 1 year after enactment
Placement, 2 percent minimum size, and 70 percent contrast rules across six packaging categories
Prohibition on express or implied flushability representations by covered entities
FTC enforcement via section 18(a)(1)(B) of the FTC Act, with rulemaking authority under section 553 of title 5, U.S.C.
State-law preemption: only requirements identical to the federal rule are allowed
Definitions of "covered product," "covered entity," "combined product," "high contrast," "label notice," "principal display panel," "State," and "symbol"
